reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is efficient object isolation in high-resolution video streams. By defining a region around the object's centroid, we create a localized processing window. This reduces the computational complexity from O(N*M) for full-frame analysis to O(n*m) where n and m are significantly smaller than N and M. The adaptive threshold introduces a safety buffer; mathematically, this is akin to defining a confidence band in statistical estimation. If the object's projected area in the image is A, the effective processing area becomes A + ε, where ε accounts for the buffer. The efficiency gain scales inversely with the square of the region-to-image-area ratio. Failure modes include occlusion leading to centroid drift and extreme zoom changes causing region undershoot/overshoot. To mitigate, recursive least-squares tracking can update the region dynamically.
